Geothermal energy harnesses heat from within the Earth providing reliable baseload power with minimal emissions
Small modular reactors are nuclear fission reactors with power output under 300 MW designed for factory fabrication and flexible deployment
Green hydrogen produced by electrolysis using renewable electricity could decarbonize hard-to-electrify sectors like steel and shipping
The levelized cost of solar photovoltaic electricity is now lower than new coal or gas power in most regions of the world
Nuclear fusion could provide virtually unlimited clean energy but sustaining the required plasma conditions remains an engineering challenge
Pumped hydroelectric storage accounts for over 90 percent of global grid-scale energy storage capacity
Building energy efficiency improvements including insulation and heat pumps can reduce heating energy consumption by 50 to 80 percent
The circular economy aims to eliminate waste by designing products for reuse repair remanufacturing and recycling
Life cycle assessment evaluates the environmental impact of a product through all stages from raw material extraction to disposal
Electric vehicles produce zero direct emissions and have lower lifetime emissions than internal combustion vehicles in most electricity grids
Offshore wind farms can generate more consistent power than onshore due to stronger and more reliable wind conditions at sea
Carbon capture and storage technology removes CO2 from industrial emissions or the atmosphere and stores it underground
Passive house design reduces heating and cooling energy by up to 90 percent through superinsulation and heat recovery ventilation
